items.claim: The risk lives in how the parser resolves external data sources, so the probe is a document that carries a DOCTYPE and an entity declaration; parameter entities are the escalation path once a plain external entity is refused.
items.body:
The risk lives in how the parser resolves external data sources, so the probe is a document that carries a DOCTYPE and an entity declaration; parameter entities are the escalation path once a plain external entity is refused.

HackTricks reference: XXE - XEE - XML External Entity (pentesting-web/xxe-xee-xml-external-entity.md)
items.disproof: Refuted if the parser rejects the DOCTYPE outright, or resolves internal entities only and never attempts to retrieve the external identifier - there is then no external resolution to test.

sources.quote:
External entities, defined with a URL, raise security concerns, particularly in the context of XML External Entity (XXE) attacks, which exploit the way XML parsers handle external data sources: <!DOCTYPE foo [ <!ENTITY myentity "value" > ]>
- XXE Detection with Parameter Entities:

items.claim: Any upload surface that accepts SVG inherits the parser exposure, because the format is XML and a crafted image is a delivery channel for external entity resolution inside the backend.
items.body:
Any upload surface that accepts SVG inherits the parser exposure, because the format is XML and a crafted image is a delivery channel for external entity resolution inside the backend.

HackTricks reference: XXE - XEE - XML External Entity (pentesting-web/xxe-xee-xml-external-entity.md)
items.disproof: Refuted if the SVG upload path rasterises or sanitises the image with no XML parsing of the stored file, or strips the DOCTYPE before any entity resolution is attempted.

sources.quote: SVG, being an XML-based format, can be exploited by attackers to submit malicious SVG images, thereby exposing the server to XXE (XML External Entity) vulnerabilities.

items.claim: An attacker-controlled out-of-band callback plus entity-derived data arriving on the error channel in the same probe is the positive confirmation that external entity resolution succeeded, not merely that the parser tolerated a DOCTYPE.
items.body:
An attacker-controlled out-of-band callback plus entity-derived data arriving on the error channel in the same probe is the positive confirmation that external entity resolution succeeded, not merely that the parser tolerated a DOCTYPE.

HackTricks reference: XXE - XEE - XML External Entity (pentesting-web/xxe-xee-xml-external-entity.md)
items.disproof: Refuted if the out-of-band endpoint never receives a request or the error channel returns no entity-derived data, since a clean rejection or a DOCTYPE-only parse produces neither.

sources.quote: This indicates a successful XXE (XML External Entity) attack, leveraging both Out of Band and Error-Based techniques to extract sensitive information.
